raw_response:
I am farming only 5 mu, and there are just two of us at home, so I cannot spread myself too wide. I will still do the wheat-maize rotation on all 5 mu, same as before. That is the safest way here. Wheat and maize both have a steady road to sell, and if one season is a little weak, the other can still make up some. I do not dare gamble on fancy things. With well water, I can save the crop when it turns dry, but pumping costs money, so I will water at the key times, not too many times. Fertilizer also costs a lot now. I would rather put a solid amount and not let the crop go hungry, but I also cannot spend carelessly. So I will do it much like the years when the harvest was decent: wheat a bit heavier, maize enough to keep it growing strong after the wheat comes off.

For wheat, I will sow in early October after the maize is cleared, using the usual local improved seed. I will put base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once around jointing if the leaves are not dark enough. Wheat matters a lot because if the stand is poor in winter, there is no fixing it later. For maize, the time is tight after wheat harvest, so I will not do deep tillage. I will harvest wheat, turn the soil quickly, and plant maize right away in mid-June. Maize grows fast in summer, so if there is rain I will save one irrigation, and if it stays dry I will water once around tasseling. I will watch weeds and insects with my own eyes and spray only when I see a real problem. That is how I keep the costs in hand.
